6
Two projectiles, X and Y, are fired into the air from the same place on level ground and reach the
same maximum height, as shown.
path of Y
path of X
ground
Projectile X is fired vertically upwards and projectile Y is fired at an angle to the horizontal.
Air resistance is negligible.
Which statement is correct?
A
X and Y are at rest at their maximum heights.
B
X and Y are fired with the same speed.
C
X and Y take the same time to return to the ground.
D
X and Y travel the same distance.

hints: Notice the diagram shows both X and Y reach the same maximum vertical height $H$ from the same level ground.
Remember vertical motion is independent of horizontal motion, with $v_y = 0$ at the top and acceleration $g$ downwards linking $H$ to initial vertical speed $u_y$ and to time.
Compare what each projectile is doing at the top: check the horizontal velocity of angled projectile Y versus vertical projectile X.
walkthrough: Start with vertical motion only: both launch from ground, reach the same height $H$, and have $v_y = 0$ at the top with $a = -g$.
Use $v_y^2 = u_y^2 - 2gH$ with $v_y = 0$ to get $u_y = \sqrt{2gH}$, so the same $H$ means X and the vertical component of Y start with the same $u_y$.
Time to the top is $t_{up} = u_y/g$ from $v_y = u_y - gt$, which is identical, and the symmetric fall to level ground gives the same total time $2t_{up}$ for both.

Rule out the others: Y keeps its horizontal velocity at the top so it is not at rest, Y must have larger launch speed because of that horizontal part, and its curved path is longer than the straight up-down path of X.
Only the equal flight time statement matches this vertical-motion argument. This is option C

A.explanation: X is momentarily at rest at the top, but Y still has horizontal velocity even though its vertical velocity is zero.

B.explanation: Both have the same initial vertical speed to reach the same height, but Y has an extra horizontal component so its resultant launch speed $\sqrt{u_x^2+u_y^2}$ is larger.

C.explanation: The same initial vertical speed and same acceleration $g$ give the same time to rise and fall back to level ground.

D.explanation: Y follows a longer curved trajectory while X travels straight up and down, so path lengths are different.
